A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MART. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original AI2-THOR and LEGENT experiments, component ablations, and trajectory case studies, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a ReALFRED evaluation and additional success/failure execution traces.

M1.justification: The retriever, Bradley-Terry objective, Trajectory Abstraction, Algorithm 1, and all five agent prompts remain unchanged. New Appendix A elaborates the existing scoring-head implementation and training pipeline without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds evaluation on ReALFRED's photorealistic, 3D-captured, multi-room environments using pick-and-place tasks. This extends the represented visual and navigation conditions beyond the retained AI2-THOR and LEGENT evaluations, although all experiments remain within the household domain.

E2.justification: PA, LP, SL, and RAP remain the evaluated baselines, with unchanged comparator membership in the original experiments. ReALFRED uses the same set. Newly discussed methods such as P-RAG are related work, not additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The added ReALFRED experiment specifies 30 training tasks with 60 subtasks and 20 testing tasks with 40 subtasks, using the existing success-rate and step-count metrics. Original task splits, model settings, and listed hyperparameters remain unchanged. The new statement about counting failures at the step limit clarifies previously unspecified handling rather than establishing a protocol revision.

E4.justification: Appendix D expands the existing plate-pickup case with successful and unsuccessful executions for both MART and similarity retrieval, including actions, reasoning, and highlighted mistakes. The component-ablation designs remain unchanged; v2's proposed additional ablations are future work.

E5.justification: Both versions state that each task is tested five times with randomized initial position and orientation. Neither adds confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests, seed details, or a changed uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: New ReALFRED Table 5 reports MART SR 0.37 versus RAP's 0.27, the highest baseline SR. Main Tables 2–4 remain unchanged. However, v1 Table 7 becomes v2 Table 8 with six altered AI2-THOR step-count entries: MART AS/AS-Sub changes from 123.19/34.07 to 78.48/21.71, while Sim.+FTM now reports lower values, 78.09/21.60. These contradict v2's main ablation table and cannot be interpreted as established performance improvements.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, Bradley-Terry loss in Equation 1, and LLaVA-Plain score in Equation 2 are unchanged. Neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs; the new grounding taxonomy is conceptual rather than formal mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: interactive preference learning produces an effective trajectory retriever, Trajectory Abstraction preserves useful information, and MART improves unseen-task success. The added benchmark supplies supporting evidence without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: v1 primarily discusses the single-trajectory/context-window limitation. v2 Section 6 additionally acknowledges missing component ablations, comparison fairness requiring adapted feature extractors, unvalidated transfer stability, and household-only coverage. Appendix D also explains how useful retrieval can still fail through execution mistakes and how similarity retrieval can succeed through independent exploration.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the promised code release with a concrete repository access statement covering the retriever, training, benchmark tasks, and simulator modifications. Appendix A adds implementation explanations, including last non-zero hidden-state scoring and max_new_tokens=1. Section 4.1.4 newly specifies failure handling for step counts. Existing hyperparameters and prompts are retained; repository availability is reported by the PDF, not independently verified.

R1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds a focused grounding discussion distinguishing visual and embodied grounding and positioning retrieval against RL, VLA, and skill-library planners, with citations including PPO, SAC, and P-RAG. ReALFRED is also newly cited. The original multimodal-retrieval review is preserved as Appendix B.2, moved from Section 2.3.

P1.justification: v2 separates the conclusion from an expanded discussion section, moves one related-work subsection to the appendix, and inserts new appendix sections before the retained material. It also updates the publication header, author spelling, and acknowledgments. Most existing prose, method descriptions, and prompts remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds ReALFRED scene illustrations and a results table, plus two substantial annotated diagrams contrasting successful and failed trajectories with actions and reasoning (Figures 8–9). Existing illustrations are retained but resized or repositioned, and main Tables 2–4 are consolidated on one page. The new comparative diagrams materially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The photorealistic multi-room evaluation, clearer implementation/access information, and balanced failure analysis improve evidential breadth and transparency. These gains are tempered by a new reporting defect: Appendix Table 8 contradicts the retained AI2-THOR step counts and reverses the MART/Sim.+FTM efficiency ranking. This weakens efficiency conclusions, but the unchanged success-rate evidence and added documentation support a limited overall improvement.
